newsitem.title: UK: Boots says no firm plans on loyalty card.
newsitem.headline: Boots says no firm plans on loyalty card.

text.p: British pharmacist and retailer Boots said on Sunday it had no firm plans to introduce a loyalty card but a spokesman confirmed trials of a card were taking place.
"The card is being tried at 29 stores in the south west of England and at 14 in the Norwich area, but no decision has been taken about introducing the scheme," a spokesman told Reuters.
The Sunday Telegraph reported Boots was to launch a loyalty card next year in an effort to boost sales and learn more about its customers.
Loyalty cards, which offer customers discounts in relation to how much they spend, have been a very popular with UK supermarket customers.
The Boots spokesman said the tests on its loyalty card, called Advantage had been "a great success, but the trials will have to be evaluated before a decision is taken to introduce it."
